messages:
maya: Quick sync — ran the soft-reserve + adaptive shard-split experiment on staging this morning. Observed fewer long-tail latencies but some throughput oscillation when multiple noisy tenants hit burst windows.
oliver: Nice, can you share the core signals you used to trigger a split?
maya: Sure. We used two signals: 1) sustained queue depth per shard > 120 requests for 5s, and 2) median latency over the shard > 60ms for 10s. Both had to be true to avoid spurious splits.
liam: Did you gate on token-cost or request-count? Those make a difference for mixed-length workloads.
maya: Request-count only for the initial experiment to keep it simple. We should add token-cost next round.
anya: What about the soft-reserve? I remember concerns about starvation when splits happen.
maya: The soft-reserve is a tiny per-tenant micro-credit (10ms-equivalent) that decays over 1s. It prevents immediate eviction during a split and gives the tenant one more attempt to join the new shard fastpath.
oliver: Can you paste the config fragment?
maya: Yes — pasted below:
```
split_thresholds:
  queue_count: 120
  median_latency_ms: 60
  sustained_secs: 5
soft_reserve:
  micro_credits: 10
  decay_ms: 1000
```
liam: Interesting. The decay feels short for long KV-cache warmups. If a request needs KV warmup it could still lose. Maybe make decay adaptive based on kv_warmup_ms metric.
maya: Agreed. We also saw ripple backpressure: when one shard split, neighbors briefly spiked because routing reshuffle caused small reassignments. That created oscillation for ~30s.
anya: Can we add a hysteresis window to prevent re-merges within X secs?
maya: We already tried a 60s cool-down for merges, but we might need asymmetric hysteresis: long cooldown for merges (120s), shorter for splits (30s). That reduces thrashing.
oliver: How did the telemetry look? Which dashboards should we watch if we roll this?
maya: Key metrics: per-shard queue_depth, shard_median_latency, split_count, merge_count, per-tenant tail P95/P99 latency, and kv_cache_misses. Also a derived metric: routing_delta_rate (changes/sec) to catch churn.
liam: Any anomalies in token-cost per-request?
maya: Token-cost increased ~2% in the first minute after split (extra routing checks) but normalized. Understood tradeoff.
anya: What's the rollout plan? I vote phased: start with 5% of staging->Canary traffic then 20% prod for low-risk clusters.
maya: Plan: Canary in two clusters for 24h, with automatic rollback if P99 increases > 15% or split_rate > baseline*3. I'll make a runbook.
oliver: For the scheduler interface, are we adding new callbacks? We should avoid expanding operator surface too much.
maya: Implemented as two optional knobs: split_policy and soft_reserve_policy, both default off. API is register_split_hook(policy_name, opts). No new blocking interfaces.
liam: Good. Also suggest adding a telemetry histogram for post-split warmup latency per-tenant. Helps tune decay.
maya: Will add.
anya: Action items?
maya: 1) add token-cost gating (liam). 2) make soft-reserve decay adaptive using kv_warmup metric (liam + maya). 3) build routing_delta_rate alarm and dashboard (oliver). 4) draft canary runbook and rollback criteria (maya).
liam: I'll start on token-cost gating PR.
oliver: I'll own dashboards/alerts.
anya: I'll review the runbook.
sre-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary-control-plane-3 at 2025-07-18T09:00Z (will notify on success/failure). :robot_face:
maya: Thanks all — will post results here after the 24h canary. :thumbsup:
